Assignment Question:
Problem statement
An enquiry counter answers the question "when is the next bus?". Departures are stored as a time in minutes past midnight together with a route code.
For each query time, report the earliest departure at or after that time. If there is none, report NONE. Finally report the first departure of the day and how many queries had no answer.
Design requirements (mandatory)
Timetable holds a TreeMap<Integer,String> and exposes add(int time, String route).
String next(int query) must use a single TreeMap navigation call - ceilingEntry - and must not loop over the entries.
firstDeparture() returns the earliest departure using firstKey.
Input format
Line 1: integer N - number of departures.
Next N lines: <time> <route>
Then a line with integer Q - number of queries.
Next Q lines: one query time each.
Output format
Q lines, each: <time> <route> for the next departure, or NONE
Then: FIRST <time> <route>
Then: MISSED <number of queries answered NONE>
Problem constraints
1 <= N <= 1000
1 <= Q <= 1000
0 <= time <= 1439
Route code is 1 to 10 characters, no spaces
If two departures share the same time, the later one in the input replaces the earlier one
Notes
A query exactly equal to a departure time is answered by that departure, not the next one.
A query after the last departure is answered NONE.
Sample input
4
360 R1
420 R2
540 R3
1140 R4
3
400
540
1200
Sample output
420 R2
540 R3
NONE
FIRST 360 R1
MISSED 1

For each query time, report the earliest departure at or after that time. If there is none, report NONE. Finally report the first departure of the day and how many queries had no answer.
Design requirements (mandatory)
Timetable holds a TreeMap<Integer,String> and exposes add(int time, String route).
String next(int query) must use a single TreeMap navigation call - ceilingEntry - and must not loop over the entries.
firstDeparture() returns the earliest departure using firstKey.
Input format
Line 1: integer N - number of departures.
Next N lines: <time> <route>
Then a line with integer Q - number of queries.
Next Q lines: one query time each.
Output format
Q lines, each: <time> <route> for the next departure, or NONE
Then: FIRST <time> <route>
Then: MISSED <number of queries answered NONE>
Problem constraints
1 <= N <= 1000
1 <= Q <= 1000
0 <= time <= 1439
Route code is 1 to 10 characters, no spaces
If two departures share the same time, the later one in the input replaces the earlier one
Notes
A query exactly equal to a departure time is answered by that departure, not the next one.
A query after the last departure is answered NONE.
Sample input
4
360 R1
420 R2
540 R3
1140 R4
3
400
540
1200
Sample output
420 R2
540 R3
NONE
FIRST 360 R1
MISSED 1
